title: ClauseLensClauseRecord
description: One German contract clause that a reviewer must flag, as stored in the ClauseLens clause database. Records live as JSONL, one record per line, in data/clauses/*.jsonl; data/manifest.json is the authoritative registry of those files. The detector enum mirrors the rule types of src/analyze.js and is cross-checked against the engine by test/clause_db.test.js.

id.description: Stable, globally unique record id. The leading segment encodes the owning slice so ids can never collide across files.

docFamily.description: Document family the clause belongs to. dach_varianten is used for clauses specific to Austrian or Swiss law; en_law_msa_sow_dpa for English-law or bilingual instruments.

clauseType.description: German label of the clause type, e.g. "Haftungsausschluss", "Schönheitsreparaturen-Klausel", "Kettenbefristung".

clauseText.description: The original clause wording as it would appear in the document, in the document's language. One clause, not a whole contract.

why.description: One plain German sentence stating why a reviewer must flag this clause.

legalBasis.description: The load-bearing norm citations, e.g. "§ 307 Abs. 1, Abs. 2 Nr. 1 BGB", "Art. 100 Abs. 1 OR", "Art. 28 Abs. 2 DSGVO".

caseLaw.description: BGH or EuGH citation, only where the decision itself carries the clause. Empty array when there is none; an invented Aktenzeichen is worse than an empty array.

otherStatutes.description: Further statutes outside the BGB/AGB core, e.g. "Art. 82 DSGVO", "§ 74 Abs. 2 HGB", "§ 14 Abs. 2 TzBfG", "Art. 269a OR".

jurisdiction.description: Legal system the clause is assessed under.

severity.description: hoch = unwirksam oder existenzgefährdend, mittel = benachteiligend aber heilbar, niedrig = Grenzfall.

detector.description: The rule in src/analyze.js that covers this clause type, or null when no rule covers the clause type at all. Whether that rule also fires on this particular wording is a separate, measurable property of the engine and is what `detectorStatus` records: `node bin/clause-db.js mapping` reports both the blind records and any record whose claim is not backed by a firing rule.

detectorStatus.description: Three states, because two collapsed a real difference. `mapped`: a rule covers this clause type AND fires on this very wording — a measurement, asserted per record against the engine, never a rate. `mapped_blind`: a rule covers the clause type but does not react to this wording (the rule exists, the wording is invisible to it; `detector` names the covering rule). `no_detector`: no rule covers the clause type at all — a counted coverage gap, and a wanted outcome of this database. `mapped_blind` is a named weakness of the rule set, not coverage: never fold it into `mapped`, and never absorb it by lowering a threshold.

evasion.description: The wording technique that hides the trap, using the same vocabulary as the stress corpus, or null when the clause is plainly drafted.
